searchText: > <@!482518216019542016> would you be able to tell which nodes are missing? <@!489256758989029405> not easily, but I guess you already found out what is causing that? Not seeing many VM pauses because of missing data now. Was able to keep up with the tip for a little while but then got a `Import starved for 199.6s, waiting for <BlockHeader #11281110 203b71d6> body` and started lagging behind 😦 <@!425615769280315392> ^ on my machine, block imports are taking 10-15s without VM pauses so once I start lagging behind it's hard to catch up oh > Not seeing many VM pauses because of missing data now. Was able to keep up with the tip for a little while but then got a `Import starved for 199.6s, waiting for <BlockHeader #11281110 203b71d6> body` and started lagging behind 😦 <@!482518216019542016> did it only get better after you synced much state in the background? was the 'import starved' due to missing state or something else? in Nethermind we skip blocks in beam sync if they fail to sync in 15 seconds we simply discard them and move to head the log says it was waiting for a block body. I suppose that was because we use a very long timeout when waiting for a block body if we'd given up earlier and asked another peer it probably would have taken a lot less than 199s ah, I see, yes we use 3 seconds > did it only get better after you synced much state in the background? this was actually with a fresh state DB. all witnesses seemed to have all the necessary nodes That "Import starved" message isn't about state, it's either headers or block bodies. <@!425615769280315392> is 10-15s to import a mainnet block normal? No, that sounds high that's what I was seeing when there were no vm pauses, and I believe my NVMe SSD has decent performance Looking over my logs, more like 7s (Using the `BeamImport` log, "total time" * "exec %"). If you're not pausing, then exec% should be 100%. yeah, I have exec% at 100% on all. some were under 10s, but most are above 10s small sample, though. only 50 or so blocks I've got a monster machine running it, with 128GB RAM, so it's plausible that I'm getting 30% faster speeds on having most of the relevant disk files in the OS buffer. You have the `rlp[rust-backend]` installed, right? At those processing times, it seems worthwhile to do another round of performance improvements yeah, with rusty-rlp maybe my AMD Ryzen processor is to blame Jason's laptop is hilariously beefy
